# Phase 17: chunked prefill into the tier

Item 2 of the [gap table](../GAP_TABLE.md)'s recommended order, and its validity note 3: until
this phase, the tier was built from an exact prefill into a full GPU cache, so the longest context
LazyKV could serve was the full cache's. Questions and design were fixed in `configs/phase17.yaml`
before any run.

## What was built

- `lazykv/tiered_prefill.py`: **layer-major prefill.** Every prompt chunk runs through layer L
  before any chunk runs through L+1 (FlexGen's schedule, arXiv 2303.06865), holding the hidden
  states of every prompt token. Only layer L's KV has to be on the GPU while layer L runs; when it
  finishes, `TieredLayer` copies it to host, builds the Quest metadata and seeds the slots, exactly
  as at the old boundary, and the buffer is reused for the next layer. Every KV byte crosses PCIe
  once, device to host. The alternative, chunk-major with earlier KV streamed back from host for
  every chunk, would move traffic that grows with the square of the context over the per-layer
  host round trip Phase 11 found to be the decode bottleneck.
- `TieredCache(tiers=...)`: the tier can be built from prebuilt layers.
- `lazykv/pinned.py`: **a bug fix found while building this.** PyTorch's caching host allocator
  rounds every pinned allocation up to the next power of two (checked on this machine with
  `torch.cuda.host_memory_stats()`). Every
  earlier phase's host store was pinned that way, using up to twice its size in RAM (timings are not
  affected). The host store is now page-locked at its real size with `cudaHostRegister`. At this
  phase's largest 3B context the difference is the gap between fitting in this laptop's 16 GB
  and not.
- `scripts/07_prefill_capacity.py`, `scripts/07_tiered_prefill_quality.py`, `scripts/analyze_phase17.py`.

**Correctness.** Each layer sees the same chunk boundaries, inputs and KV prefix as in the
chunk-major prefill, so the result is the same, bit for bit: `tests/test_tiered_prefill.py` checks
the logits, the host store, the metadata, the seeded slots and 40 decode steps after it, for three
chunk sizes and for rungs 6, 7 and 8. A check on the real 1B model at 8K gave identical logits and
identical decoded tokens. Question 3 below repeats the check on 90 NIAH decodes of the 3B model.

## 1. Capacity: the longest context each prefill reaches

One NIAH prompt per cell, prefilled and decoded (32 tokens, rung 6 at a 12.5% budget for the tier),
each cell in a fresh process with the allocator capped at the dedicated VRAM free at startup, so a
cell that does not fit fails with OOM instead of spilling. Ladders stop at a method's first failure.

| Model | Full cache: longest that ran | Full cache: first failure | Tiered prefill: longest that ran | Prefill peak, tiered ÷ full | Prefill time, tiered ÷ full |
| --- | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: |
| 1B | 96K | 127K | 127K (top of the ladder; no failure reached) | 0.71–0.82 | 1.01–1.05 |
| 3B | 32K | 48K | 64K (top of the ladder; no failure reached) | 0.58–0.68 | 0.94–1.05 |

| 1B | 32K | tiered | ran | 1.00 | 2.99 | 2.60 | 0.90 | 6.7 | 51.4 | 16 |

| 3B | 24K | full | ran | 2.62 | 5.18 | 4.98 |  | 10.4 | 48.4 | 0 |
| 3B | 24K | tiered | ran | 2.62 | 3.22 | 2.81 | 2.54 | 10.8 | 104.1 | 32 |

- **The tier now holds contexts the full cache cannot prefill at all.** The 1B model reaches the top of its
  128K context window (a 127K-token prompt plus the decode). On the 3B model with 4-bit weights the tier runs at
  65,536 tokens, whose full KV alone
  (7.00 GiB) is more than this card has free; the tier's
  prefill peaked at 4.82 GiB.
  Neither tiered ladder found its limit; the 3B one stopped where its host store
  (6.60 GiB pinned) takes a large share of the
  machine's 16 GB, which is the next wall.
- **Prefill costs the same.** Tiered over full prefill time is
  1.01–1.05
  on the 1B model and
  0.94–1.05
  on the 3B, single runs each. The boundary work (D2H, metadata, seeding) is a small part of it.
- **Peak VRAM still grows with context, more slowly.** What remains is the dense layers' full KV
  (Quest's first two layers, attended densely in decode), the hidden states of every prompt token,
  and one layer's KV, held twice while `TieredLayer` stacks it into blocks. Each could be cut
  further (hidden states and the stack to host, or in pieces); none is needed to reach the ladders' tops.
- **Decode over the tier is as slow as it always was**:
  2.1–2.6×
  the full cache's per-token time on the 1B model and
  2.2–2.8×
  on the 3B, for the reason Phases 6 to 11 measured: the per-layer host round trip.
  Tiered prefill does not change decode at all, as the bit-identity test requires.
- "Shared beyond pins" is the process's shared GPU memory minus its pinned host store and minus the
  full-cache cells' baseline. The remainder in tiered cells is the small pinned staging and index
  buffers, which still go through the rounding allocator; nothing spilled.

## 3. Quality beyond the full cache's limit

NIAH (single, multi-key, multi-value; five depths; three samples) on the 3B model. At 32K, the full
cache's longest context, both the full cache and the tier ran, so the tier's numbers there pair
with a reference. At 64K the full cache cannot run, so the tier's score is an absolute accuracy and
is not a retention.

_not measured_

## What this phase does not show

- Two models, one prompt per capacity cell, one run per cell: the capacity table answers "does it
  run", and its timings are single measurements.
- The tier's own limits were not found: the 1B ladder stops at the model's context window and the
  3B ladder at 64K, chosen to keep the host store well inside 16 GB of RAM.
- No host tier below RAM (no SSD), so host RAM is the bound on context.
